title: Affine-local characterization of flat families with geometric complete-intersection fibres
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. For a field $k$, say a scheme locally of finite type over $k$ is a local complete intersection over $k$ if it has an affine open cover by spectra of finitely generated $k$-algebras which are local complete intersections in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-complete-intersection-over-field]; the empty scheme is allowed. The following conditions are equivalent. (1) The morphism $f$ is flat [def-weil-flat-morphism], locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], and for every algebraically closed field $\Omega$ and geometric point $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to Y$ [def-weil-geometric-point] its geometric fibre, the fibre product $X\times_Y\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ [def-pc-fibre-product] [def-weil-geometric-fibre], is a local complete intersection over $\Omega$. (2) For every affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq Y$ and every affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}B\subseteq X$ with $f(U)\subseteq V$, the induced map $A\to B$ is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] and of finite presentation [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra], and for every prime ideal $\mathfrak p\subset A$ the fibre ring $B\otimes_A\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] is a local complete intersection over $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$. (3) There exist an affine open cover $Y=\bigcup_a V_a$, $V_a=\operatorname{Spec}A_a$, and for each $a$ an affine open cover $f^{-1}(V_a)=\bigcup_b U_{ab}$, $U_{ab}=\operatorname{Spec}B_{ab}$, such that each induced map $A_a\to B_{ab}$ is flat and of finite presentation and every fibre ring $B_{ab}\otimes_{A_a}\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is a local complete intersection over $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ for every prime $\mathfrak p\subset A_a$.

source.place: Tag 01UD (lemma-syntomic-characterize), conditions (1), (2), (4); Tag 01UC (definition-syntomic); Tag 01UE (lemma-syntomic-locally-standard-syntomic) and Tag 01UF (lemma-syntomic-flat-fibres). Ring syntomicity is precisely the three written ring conditions by Algebra Tag 00SL (definition-lci). The geometric-fibre formulation uses Algebra Tag 00SJ (lemma-lci-field-change), algebra.tex, and Morphisms lemma-local-complete-intersection.

proof.text: First fix an affine pair $U=\operatorname{Spec}B\subseteq X$, $V=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq Y$ with $f(U)\subseteq V$, and a map $\operatorname{Spec}k\to V$ from a field. Put $X_k=X\times_Y\operatorname{Spec}k$. By [lem-weil-pbc-open-preimage-fibre-product], the inverse image $U_k$ of $U$ under $X_k\to X$ is an open subscheme and is the pullback of $U\to X$ along that projection. The universal property [def-pc-fibre-product] identifies it with $U\times_V\operatorname{Spec}k$: a map into either object is exactly a map into $U$ and a map into $\operatorname{Spec}k$ whose composites into $Y$ agree; both composites factor through the open $V$, where agreement is equivalent. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] gives $U_k\cong\operatorname{Spec}(B\otimes_A k)$ over $k$. Inverse images of a covering family cover: the inverse image of its union is the union of its inverse images. We use these chart identifications and this covering observation below.

source.place: Tags 01JR (lemma-open-fibre-product), 01I4 (lemma-fibre-product-affine-schemes); restriction and pullback universal properties.

proof.text: Assume (1), and fix any affine pair $U,V$ as in step 1. By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-affine-criterion], $A\to B$ is flat. By [lem-weil-pbc-lfp-affine-opens-finite-presentation], it is of finite presentation. For each prime $\mathfrak p\subset A$, [lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-base-change-composition] (1), with base change $A\to\kappa(\mathfrak p)$, shows that $S=B\otimes_A\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is a finitely presented $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$-algebra (interchanging the two tensor factors). In particular it is finitely generated: the images of the finitely many polynomial variables in a presentation [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra] generate it.

source.place: Tags 01U5 (lemma-flat-characterize), (1) implies (2), and 01TQ (lemma-locally-finite-presentation-characterize), (1) implies (2); Algebra Tag 05G5 (lemma-base-change-finiteness), (4).

proof.text: Continue with (1), $U,V,\mathfrak p,S$ from step 2. Choose an algebraic closure $\Omega$ of $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ using [def-weil-algebraic-closure]. The point of $V$ corresponding to $\mathfrak p$ and the field inclusion define a geometric point $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to Y$ by [def-weil-geometric-point]. Its fibre $X_\Omega$ has an affine cover by finitely generated local-complete-intersection $\Omega$-algebras by (1). Step 1 identifies its affine open $U_\Omega$ with $\operatorname{Spec}(B\otimes_A\Omega)$. Applying [lem-trf-lci-affine-open-locality] to this open proves that $B\otimes_A\Omega$ is a local complete intersection over $\Omega$. There is an $\Omega$-algebra isomorphism $(B\otimes_A\kappa(\mathfrak p))\otimes_{\kappa(\mathfrak p)}\Omega\cong B\otimes_A\Omega$, sending $(b\otimes t)\otimes u$ to $b\otimes tu$, with inverse $b\otimes u\mapsto(b\otimes1)\otimes u$; the balanced relations show these are well-defined inverses. The converse direction of [lem-weil-pbc-lci-field-change], applicable because $S$ is of finite type by step 2, proves that $S$ is a local complete intersection over $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$. Together with step 2 this proves (2).

source.place: Tag 00SJ (lemma-lci-field-change), descent along the algebraic closure; Morphisms Tag 01UG (lemma-local-complete-intersection) for the arbitrary affine open in the geometric fibre.

proof.text: Condition (2) implies (3): choose an affine open cover of $Y$ and, for each member $V_a$, an affine open cover of the open subscheme $f^{-1}(V_a)$, using the local affine property of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. Each source member is an affine open of $X$ mapping into $V_a$, so (2) supplies exactly the three required properties. If an inverse image is empty, its cover may be empty.

source.place: Tag 01UD (lemma-syntomic-characterize), (2) implies (4), with ring syntomicity expanded as Algebra Tag 00SL (definition-lci).

proof.text: Assume (3). For every chart $U_{ab}\to V_a$, its flat coordinate map makes the chart morphism flat by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map-iff-flat-affine]. For any $x\in X$, choose $a,b$ with $x\in U_{ab}$. The stalk map of this restricted morphism is the stalk map $\mathcal O_{Y,f(x)}\to\mathcal O_{X,x}$, since restricting a sheaf to an open neighbourhood leaves its stalk unchanged. This map is flat, so $f$ is flat by the pointwise definition [def-weil-flat-morphism]. The same affine pair around $x$ has a finitely presented coordinate map by (3), so $f$ is of finite presentation at $x$ by [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. This holds for every $x$, proving that $f$ is locally of finite presentation.

source.place: Tags 01U5 (lemma-flat-characterize) and 01TQ (lemma-locally-finite-presentation-characterize), the covering-to-pointwise directions written from the definitions.

proof.text: Still assume (3). Fix any geometric point $\bar y:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to Y$ and let $y$ be its image. Choose $a$ with $y\in V_a$. By [def-weil-geometric-point], $\bar y$ gives a field extension $\kappa(y)\to\Omega$; with $\mathfrak p\subset A_a$ corresponding to $y$, this is $\kappa(\mathfrak p)\to\Omega$. For every $b$, set $S_b=B_{ab}\otimes_{A_a}\kappa(\mathfrak p)$. By (3), $S_b$ is a local complete intersection and hence a finitely generated $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$-algebra by [def-weil-pbc-complete-intersection-over-field]. The forward direction of [lem-weil-pbc-lci-field-change] implies that $S_b\otimes_{\kappa(\mathfrak p)}\Omega$ is a finitely generated local-complete-intersection $\Omega$-algebra. The tensor formulas in step 3 identify it with $B_{ab}\otimes_{A_a}\Omega$. Since $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to Y$ factors through $V_a$, the first projection $X\times_Y\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to X$ has image in the open $f^{-1}(V_a)$ (its composite with $f$ equals the composite of the second projection with $\bar y$, which lands in $V_a$); as the $U_{ab}$ cover $f^{-1}(V_a)$, their inverse images cover $X\times_Y\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$, and step 1 identifies each of them with the spectrum of the corresponding algebra. They form an affine open cover of $X\times_Y\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$. This cover makes the fibre locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] and a local complete intersection in the sense stipulated in the item. An empty fibre has the empty cover, so needs no nonemptiness assumption. With step 5 this proves (1), closing the cycle (1)$\Rightarrow$(2)$\Rightarrow$(3)$\Rightarrow$(1).

lean.statement: theorem syntomic_geometric_fibres_affine_criterion {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) : ((Flat f ∧ LocallyOfFinitePresentation f ∧ ∀ (Ω : Type u) [Field Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω] (ybar : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ Y), IsLocalCompleteIntersectionOver Ω (Limits.pullback f ybar) (Limits.pullback.snd f ybar)) ↔ (∀ (V : Y.Opens) (hV : IsAffineOpen V) (U : X.Opens) (hU : IsAffineOpen U) (hUV : U ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ V), IsSyntomicAffineChart f V U hUV)) ∧ ((∀ (V : Y.Opens) (hV : IsAffineOpen V) (U : X.Opens) (hU : IsAffineOpen U) (hUV : U ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ V), IsSyntomicAffineChart f V U hUV) ↔ (∃ (I : Type u) (V : I → Y.Opens), (∀ i, IsAffineOpen (V i)) ∧ (∀ y : Y, ∃ i, y ∈ V i) ∧ ∀ i, ∃ (J : Type u) (U : J → X.Opens), (∀ j, IsAffineOpen (U j)) ∧ (∀ x : X, x ∈ f ⁻¹ᵁ V i → ∃ j, x ∈ U j) ∧ ∀ j, ∃ hUV : U j ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ V i, IsSyntomicAffineChart f (V i) (U j) hUV))
